audit.note: the search query and the picked product's title travel with the dialog's events

deviations.what: the four Inputs are the sample: not editable, not enabled, editable, and editable with a value help. All four carry their type, placeholder, enabled and editable flags 1:1; only the fourth has any behaviour.

handleValueHelp loads Dialog.fragment.xml once (Fragment.load, kept as a view dependent) and opens it. The port expresses it as a core:FragmentDefinition shown through client->popup_display and served per request, which is what lets the backend filter its list. The controller also remembers which input asked (this.inputId) so _handleValueHelpClose can write back into it - here only one Input has a value help, so the picked title goes into its bound field directly.

Thin frontend: _handleValueHelpSearch builds a Name Contains filter and calls filter() on the dialog's items binding; the port filters the ABAP table it sends (app 298 idiom). Both close paths clear the filter for the next open, as the original does.

the StandardListItem's icon binds PICURL where the fragment writes {ProductPicUrl} - the same field under the ABAP component name, with the sanctioned host absolutization onto sdk.openui5.org. Its description binds {Productid} in the sample, a lower-case 'id' the mock does not carry (the field is ProductId), so upstream that line is empty; the port binds the field the mock really has.
